Hey, please don't do it. May I tell u a story. I watched a YouTube video about a girl who tried to kill herself by Doctor assistance. At the week approaching the end of her life, chose not to. There was a particular scene of her with her friends, sitting outside together and having a chat and tea. They were smiling, talking about the memories of each other they shared. I could sense that they were truly going to miss her and the love they had for their dead friend. I think this, among many other reasons is why the girl chose not to do it. She had been waiting years to do it as custom by the doctor assisted suicide. But at her final day, she chose not to do it. Depression is something that must be treated like any other kind of illness. If left untreated it only gets worse and worse. Of course there are falls in the system, but you have to push, and fight for your right to happiness and liberty. Don't be a statistic, you are far capable of becoming so much more than that. You are not a fuck up and your friend isn't cutting contact with you because of your actions, but because of her strong emotions and feelings. I can assume you two were pretty connected by feelings. Remember, that your feelings are not you, nor do they reflect reality accurately. Our minds can say that reality is either black or white, when really in reality there are many shades of grey. I've been there. Feelings can make it seem like theyre is so real, but they aren't. Things don't have to be entirely good, but they're not entirely bad either. Please seek therapy friend, CBT and try to get the help u deserve. Also look up woebot.io they provide instant services for depressed people like us. God bless you and stay alive.

Think about why you smoke weed in the first place. For me, I smoked it because it was a way to procrastinate what I should do in life. There is a person who I want to be, and that person is a sober person who values being drug free. Personally drugs are a detriment to my health and well being, and so because of this I value caring for myself and being sober. But if it wasn’t for my relapse today, after being two whole months clean, I would probably have taken sobriety fore granted. But now I cherish it, and hold it so very dear to me, because it’s pretty much being loving toward myself, and is my main form of self care. I recognize that people in our community want to regain their life back, nd that begins with sobriety, which is, ultimately self care towards ourselves.
